findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default (unless account-level default encryption applies), violating the principle that encryption at rest should be the default state.

findings.issue_category: missing access control / public access block
findings.description: No ACL or public access block is set, and no bucket policy restricting access is present, leaving the bucket at risk of overly permissive default access; also lacks any explicit private ACL setting seen in sibling buckets.
The bucket has 'private' ACL but no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so data at rest is not encrypted by default, exposing sensitive ledger/financial export data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket despite storing model artifacts, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so operational runbook content (which can contain sensitive infrastructure details) is stored unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: invalid/malformed ACL leading to unintended access
findings.description: The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid canned ACL (should likely be 'log-delivery-write-only'); a malformed or incorrect ACL can result in unintended access behavior or apply failures that mask the intended restrictive configuration for this sensitive audit-log bucket.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption at rest for uploaded object
findings.description: The object is uploaded to reports_archive, a bucket lacking default encryption, meaning this potentially sensitive vendor roster file (vendor-roster.xlsx) is stored without encryption at rest.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recovery, increasing risk of accidental or malicious irreversible data loss for archived reports.

findings.issue_category: force_destroy enabled on audit log bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket permits deletion of security audit logs along with the bucket, undermining the integrity and availability guarantees expected of an audit trail store.
